chunks: Qarqara, from Muhammad ibn Khalaf, from al-Hasan ibn Salih ibn al-Aswad, from Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-Abbas al-Hamadani, from Ammar al-Dahni, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asked: 'How long do you reckon the stay of al-Sufyani among you will be?' I replied: 'The duration of a woman's pregnancy, nine months.' He said: 'I do not know you, O people of Kufa.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْكُوفَةِ: The people of Kufa, a major city in Iraq often referenced in Shia eschatological traditions.
key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيُّ: Al-Sufyani, a specific leader from the tribe of Banu Umayya who appears before the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi.

ai.seo_question: How long will the rule of Sufyani last according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) engages the people of Kufa regarding the duration of the Sufyani’s rule, a pivotal prelude to the Mahdi’s reappearance. The companions’ answer of 'nine months,' drawing a parallel to human gestation, elicits the Imam’s remark, 'I do not think you know, O people of Kufa,' which Shia scholars interpret as either a correction to a longer duration or an indication that their understanding of the Sufyani’s impact was superficial. This exchange highlights the Kufans' specific eschatological expectations and the nuanced scholarly debate surrounding the timeline of the Sufyani’s emergence.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 477 - It is narrated from Qarqara from Muhammad bin Khalaf from Hasan bin Salih bin Aswad from Abdul Jabbar bin Abbas Hamadani from Ammar Dahni that he said:

Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s) asked: “How long will the rule of Sufyani last?” I replied: “For the duration of a normal human pregnancy (nine months).” Imam (a.s) said: “O people of Kufa, how knowledgeable you are about this matter!”
